subject: math
title: Adding and Subtracting to 1000
seo_title: Grade 3 Adding and Subtracting to 1000 Worksheets: Regrouping and Mental Math (BC)
meta_desc: Free Grade 3 math worksheets on adding and subtracting to 1000, matched to the BC curriculum: facts to 20, mental strategies, column addition and subtraction with regrouping, subtracting across zeros and BC word problems. 100 questions with an answer key.
key_big: Know your facts to 20. Line up hundreds, tens and ones. Regroup when you need to.
key_sub: Adding: if a column makes 10 or more, regroup 1 into the next column. Subtracting: if the top digit is smaller, regroup 1 from the next column. Check: add back what you took away.
body_html:
Start with facts to 20

Big sums are built from small facts. Make ten to add. Think addition to subtract.

For 13 − 5, think: 5 + what = 13? 5 + 8 = 13, so 13 − 5 = 8.

Split into hundreds, tens and ones

Split both numbers. Add the hundreds, the tens and the ones. Then put the parts back together.

Mental strategies: jump and compensate

On an open number line, start at the first number. Jump the hundreds, then the tens, then the ones.

Compensate

What is 375 + 198?

198 is 2 less than 200. 375 + 200 = 575. You added 2 too many, so take 2 away: 575 − 2 = 573.

Answer: 573

Column addition: regroup when a column makes 10 or more

Put ones under ones, tens under tens and hundreds under hundreds. Start with the ones on the right. If a column makes 10 or more, write the ones digit and regroup 1 into the next column.

Column subtraction: regroup when the top digit is smaller

Always take the bottom digit from the top digit. If the top digit is smaller, regroup 1 from the next column as 10.

Across zeros: if there are 0 tens, regroup 1 hundred as 10 tens first. Then regroup 1 ten as 10 ones. The 0 tens become 9 tens.

Check with the inverse

Is 500 − 168 = 332 right?

Add back what you took away: 332 + 168 = 500. You get the starting number, so it is right.

Answer: Yes

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Not regrouping (367 + 258 = 515)Write the regrouped 1 in the next column and add it in
Taking the smaller digit from the larger one (452 − 178 = 326, 13 − 5 = 12)Always take the bottom digit from the top digit. Regroup when the top is smaller
Making the 0 tens into 10 tens (500 − 168 = 342)One ten moves to the ones, so 10 tens become 9 tens
Lining up the columns wrongly (346 + 52 = 866)Line up the ones on the right: 346 + 52 = 398

faq.q: What does Grade 3 learn about adding and subtracting in the BC math curriculum?
faq.a: Under Computational fluency, Grade 3 students add and subtract to 1000 and become fluent with addition and subtraction facts to 20. They use mental strategies, base ten blocks, number lines and the column method.

faq.q: What is regrouping in Grade 3 math?
faq.a: Regrouping means trading 10 of one place for 1 of the next, such as 10 ones for 1 ten. Older books call it carrying or borrowing.

faq.q: How do you subtract across zeros, like 500 − 168?
faq.a: Regroup 1 hundred as 10 tens, then 1 ten as 10 ones. 500 becomes 4 hundreds, 9 tens and 10 ones, so 500 − 168 = 332.

faq.q: Do Grade 3 students in BC write a provincial math test?
faq.a: No. BC students write the Foundation Skills Assessment (FSA) in Grades 4 and 7. Strong adding and subtracting in Grade 3 is a good base for it.

sets.title: Warm-up: addition and subtraction facts to 20

items.q: Fill the top frame first. What is 9 + 5?
items.e: 9 needs 1 more to make 10. Take 1 from the 5: 4 are left. 10 + 4 = 14.

items.q: Fill the top frame first. What is 8 + 7?
items.e: 8 needs 2 more to make 10. Take 2 from the 7: 5 are left. 10 + 5 = 15.

items.q: Fill the top frame first. What is 7 + 6?
items.e: 7 needs 3 more to make 10. Take 3 from the 6: 3 are left. 10 + 3 = 13.

items.q: Fill the top frame first. What is 9 + 8?
items.e: 9 needs 1 more to make 10. Take 1 from the 8: 7 are left. 10 + 7 = 17.

items.q: How many more counters fill both frames to make 20?
items.e: The frames hold 20. There are 13 counters. 13 + 7 = 20, so 7 more make 20.

items.q: Use double 7. What is 7 + 8?
items.e: Double 7 is 14. 8 is 1 more than 7, so add 1: 15.

What is 12 − 5?
What is 16 − 9?
Count up from 8 to 13. What is 13 − 8?
items.e: Count the steps from 8 to 13: there are 5. 8 + 5 = 13, so 13 − 8 = 5.

items.q: Count up from 9 to 17. What is 17 − 9?
items.e: Count the steps from 9 to 17: there are 8. 9 + 8 = 17, so 17 − 9 = 8.

items.q: What number goes in the box? 8 + ? = 15
items.e: Think: 8 and how many more make 15? 8 + 2 = 10, 10 + 5 = 15. 2 + 5 = 7. (23 adds 8 + 15 instead.)

items.q: What number goes in the box? ? + 6 = 13
items.e: 13 − 6 = 7. Check: 7 + 6 = 13. (19 adds instead of taking away.)

items.q: Which fact is in the same fact family as 7 + 9 = 16?
items.e: A fact family uses the same three numbers: 7, 9 and 16. 16 − 9 = 7 uses all three.

items.q: 9 + 6 = 15. Use this fact. What is 90 + 60?
items.e: 9 tens + 6 tens = 15 tens. 15 tens is 150.

items.q: 14 − 8 = 6. Use this fact. What is 140 − 80?
items.e: 14 tens − 8 tens = 6 tens. 6 tens is 60.

items.q: Wei saw 8 bald eagles by the river in the morning and 7 more in the afternoon. How many bald eagles did he see?
items.e: Put the two groups together, so add. 8 + 2 = 10, 10 + 5 = 15. 8 + 7 = 15.

items.q: Zara had 13 stickers. She gave 5 stickers to a friend. How many stickers does she have now?
items.e: Giving away means subtract. 13 − 3 = 10, 10 − 2 = 8. 13 − 5 = 8.

items.q: Ava says 15 − 7 = 12. What did she do wrong?
items.e: 15 − 7 = 8. Ava saw 5 and 7 and took the smaller digit from the larger one: 7 − 5 = 2, so she wrote 12. Think addition instead: 7 + 8 = 15. She did 7 − 5.

items.q: Which one does NOT make 20?
items.e: 11 + 8 = 19, not 20. So 11 + 8 does not make 20. 12 + 8, 15 + 5 and 10 + 10 all make 20.

items.e: Only the hundreds change. 5 hundreds + 3 hundreds = 8 hundreds. 527 + 300 = 827.

items.q: Count on to find the difference. What is 512 − 497?
items.e: The numbers are close, so count on from 497. 497 + 3 = 500, then 500 + 12 = 512. 3 + 12 = 15. So 512 − 497 = 15.

items.q: Count on to find the difference. What is 804 − 788?
items.e: The numbers are close, so count on from 788. 788 + 12 = 800, then 800 + 4 = 804. 12 + 4 = 16. So 804 − 788 = 16.

items.q: 199 is 1 less than 200. What is 538 + 199?
items.e: Add 200, then take away the extra 1. 538 + 200 = 738. 738 − 1 = 737.

items.q: 398 is 2 less than 400. What is 426 + 398?
items.e: Add 400, then take away the extra 2. 426 + 400 = 826. 826 − 2 = 824.

items.q: 298 is 2 less than 300. What is 645 − 298?
items.e: Take away 300. You took away 2 too many, so add 2 back. 645 − 300 = 345. 345 + 2 = 347.

items.q: 99 is 1 less than 100. What is 723 − 99?
items.e: Take away 100. You took away 1 too many, so add 1 back. 723 − 100 = 623. 623 + 1 = 624.

items.q: A BC Ferries sailing to Nanaimo carried 386 passengers on Saturday morning. The next sailing carried 457 passengers. How many passengers did the two sailings carry?
items.e: Put the two sailings together, so add. 386 + 457 = 843. Check: 843 − 457 = 386.

items.q: Students counted 248 salmon in a creek on Monday and 175 salmon on Tuesday. How many salmon did they count in the two days?
items.e: Put the two days together, so add. 248 + 175 = 423. Check: 423 − 175 = 248.

items.q: At our school’s Terry Fox Run, Grade 3 raised $165 and Grade 2 raised $278. How much money did the two grades raise?
items.e: Put the two amounts together, so add. $165 + $278 = $443. Check: $443 − $278 = $165.

items.q: On Saturday, 356 people rode the Skyride up Grouse Mountain in the morning and 287 people rode it in the afternoon. How many people rode it that day?
items.e: Put the morning and the afternoon together, so add. 356 + 287 = 643. Check: 643 − 287 = 356.

items.q: On a trip in BC, the Singh family drove 276 km on Friday and 358 km on Saturday. How far did they drive in the two days?
items.e: Put the two parts of the trip together, so add. 276 + 358 = 634. Check: 634 − 358 = 276.

items.q: A ferry can carry 600 passengers. 437 passengers are on board. How many more passengers can get on?
items.e: Find how many more fit, so subtract. 600 − 437 = 163. Check: 163 + 437 = 600.

items.q: Last fall, volunteers counted 812 salmon in a river. This fall they counted 547. How many fewer salmon did they count this fall?
items.e: How many fewer means find the difference, so subtract. 812 − 547 = 265. Check: 265 + 547 = 812.

items.q: Volunteers counted 436 coho salmon and 289 chinook salmon at a counting fence. How many more coho salmon did they count?
items.e: How many more means find the difference, so subtract. 436 − 289 = 147. Check: 147 + 289 = 436.

items.q: Emma’s chapter book has 304 pages. She has read 128 pages. How many pages are left?
items.e: Find what is left, so subtract. 304 − 128 = 176. Check: 176 + 128 = 304.

items.q: The class wants $500 for a field trip to the Vancouver Aquarium. It has $368 so far. How much more money does it need?
items.e: Find the difference, so subtract. $500 − $368 = $132. Check: $132 + $368 = $500.

items.q: The school library has 750 books. 286 books are checked out. How many books are on the shelves?
items.e: Books checked out are taken away, so subtract. 750 − 286 = 464. Check: 464 + 286 = 750.

items.q: Nadia had some hockey cards. She got 135 more for her birthday. Now she has 402 cards. How many cards did she have at the start?
items.e: Work backwards. Take away the 135 that were added: 402 − 135 = 267. Check: 267 + 135 = 402.

items.q: A ferry stopped at Salt Spring Island and 168 passengers got off. Now 279 passengers are on the ferry. How many passengers were on the ferry before the stop?
items.e: Work backwards. Add back the 168 that were taken away: 279 + 168 = 447. Check: 447 − 168 = 279.

items.q: The school’s Terry Fox Run goal is $800. Grade 3 raised $276 and Grade 4 raised $348. How much more money is needed?
items.e: Step 1, money raised: $276 + $348 = $624. Step 2, money still needed: $800 − $624 = $176.

items.q: A trail through the cedar trees in Stanley Park is 900 m long. Ethan walked 345 m, rested, then walked 278 m. How many metres are left?
items.e: Step 1, metres walked: 345 + 278 = 623. Step 2, metres left: 900 − 623 = 277.

items.q: A ferry to the Gulf Islands left with 534 passengers. At the first island, 185 passengers got off and 98 passengers got on. How many passengers are on the ferry now?
items.e: Step 1, after the passengers got off: 534 − 185 = 349. Step 2, after the new passengers got on: 349 + 98 = 447.

items.q: On Saturday, students counted 268 salmon in a creek. On Sunday they counted 149 more than on Saturday. How many salmon did they count on the two days?
items.e: Step 1, Sunday’s salmon: 268 + 149 = 417. Step 2, both together: 268 + 417 = 685.

items.q: In the first hour, 386 people got on the SkyTrain at one station. In the second hour, 127 fewer people got on. How many people got on in the two hours?
items.e: Step 1, the second hour: 386 − 127 = 259. Step 2, both together: 386 + 259 = 645.

items.q: Liam read 236 pages over Spring Break. Lucas read 148 more pages than Liam. How many pages did they read together?
items.e: Step 1, the second reader’s pages: 236 + 148 = 384. Step 2, both together: 236 + 384 = 620.

items.q: The ferry from Tsawwassen had 905 passengers on board. 368 of them were in cars. The rest walked on. How many passengers walked on?
items.e: Take the passengers in cars away from all the passengers, so subtract. 905 − 368 = 537. Check: 537 + 368 = 905.
